body:
`test-dotnet` CI fails with `NameError: name 'package_name' is not defined` because `_set_dotnet_version` referenced `package_name` without it being a parameter, while the call site already passed it as a third argument.

## Change

- Added `package_name` as a third parameter to `_set_dotnet_version` (with default `"Parquet.Net"` matching the existing call site default), aligning the signature with how it was already being called:

```python
# Before
def _set_dotnet_version(cli_dir, version):
    ...
    escaped_name = re.escape(package_name)  # NameError

# After
def _set_dotnet_version(cli_dir, version, package_name="Parquet.Net"):
    ...
    escaped_name = re.escape(package_name)  # works; also allows ParquetSharp override
```

author: la14-1
body:
**Why:** Users cannot reconnect to openclaw or zeroclaw sessions — `spawn enter` throws a "corrupted history" security error because the stored launch commands fail `validateLaunchCmd()` validation.

## Root Cause

`validateLaunchCmd()` uses an allowlist of three segment patterns (source, export PATH, binary). Two agents produce launch commands that don't match:

1. **openclaw**: `launchCmd()` contained inline `if`/`while`/`$()` shell logic for gateway startup — fails the preamble allowlist
2. **zeroclaw**: `launchCmd()` used `export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"` with double quotes — the validation regex doesn't include `"` in its character class

## Fix

- **openclaw**: Remove redundant inline gateway startup from `launchCmd()`. The gateway is already supervised by systemd (`Restart=always`) + cron heartbeat, both set up during `preLaunch`. The inline wait was unnecessary for reconnect.
- **zeroclaw**: Remove quotes from `export PATH=` value — unnecessary since the value has no spaces.
- **tests**: Update zeroclaw test case to match the actual stored command (with `export PATH=` segment).
- **version**: Bump to 0.12.25.

Verified: both commands now pass `validateLaunchCmd()`. All 1408 tests pass, zero lint errors.

-- refactor/code-health

This change adds explicit inventory payload logging on the upload path so failures can be correlated with the exact data sent.

  - Added targeted detection in `CoflWebSocket::send_message` for outbound `uploadInventory` messages.
  - Logs the extracted payload both to normal logs and `inventory_upload.log` at the exact send boundary.

### Motivation
- Mejorar la estabilidad y la experiencia de uso en las pantallas principales (check-in, tutor y reporte) para uso en sala y móvil sin tocar el flujo de login.
- Reducir fricción y errores comunes (envíos dobles, tokens inválidos, confusión tras registro) y aportar reportes/CSV más robustos para consumo en Excel en castellano.

### Description
- `checkin.html`: mensajes claros por escenario (ya registrado, sesión cerrada/QR deshabilitado, token no encontrado, error de red), bloqueo de doble envío con botón que muestra `Registrando…`, estilos de alerta (`.msg.ok`, `.msg.err`, `.msg.info`), inputs y botón más grandes para móvil, limpieza post-registro que mantiene el correo y limpia solo el nombre, sugerencia de nombre por `localStorage` por correo (`LS_LAST_BY_EMAIL`) y foco optimizado; no se modifica el login ni RPCs existentes y no se renombraron IDs.
- `tutor.html`: se añadió un contenedor nuevo `#liveList` y estilos asociados para mostrar participantes (Nombre + Correo + Hora) bajo el contador `#liveCount`, se integra la lectura en el mismo polling (cada 5s) usando una consulta a `asistencias_v2` y se sanitiza texto con `escapeHtml`; cuando la sesión finaliza se detiene el polling y se mantiene el resumen/total.
- `reporte.html`: añadí un chip/selector de fechas rápidas (Hoy / Esta semana / Últimos 30 días) que actúa sobre los datos ya cargados, botones tipo chip sincronizados con el `select` y la función `cargar()`, export CSV reforzado con BOM UTF-8, escapado de comillas y saltos de línea y selector de separador (`;` por defecto o `,`), `downloadCSVFile` ahora acepta separador; se corrigió la acción del botón `Aplicar` para invocar `cargar()` y se mantuvo la analítica (torta, barras, heatmap) redibujándose con los datos filtrados.

### Testing
- Se verificó la sintaxis de todos los scripts embebidos con `node --check` extrayendo los `<script>` de `checkin.html`, `tutor.html` y `reporte.html`, y las tres páginas pasaron la verificación sin errores.

body:
Companion crashes on boot with `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file` because Docker volume mounts at `/config` may be root-owned — the build-time `chown` doesn't carry over to mounted volumes.

### Changes

- **`entrypoint.sh`**: `chown -R companion:companion /config` while still root, before `gosu` drops privileges. Warns on failure instead of silently swallowing.
- **`job_store.py`**: `JobStore.__init__` now creates the DB parent directory defensively and fails fast with a clear `PermissionError` (including uid + path) instead of falling through to a cryptic sqlite3 error.

```python
# Before: opaque crash
sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file

# After: actionable diagnostic
PermissionError: Database directory /config is not writable (uid=999). Check volume mount permissions.
```

## Summary

Adds a self-contained local telemetry playground (Kind + Prometheus + Grafana + dashboards + traffic generators) and aligns it with the **injected OTel Collector sidecar** introduced by #342.

## Architecture (re-aligned on #342)

Every DocumentDB pod runs a **per-pod OTel Collector sidecar** injected by the CNPG sidecar-injector plugin (`spec.monitoring.enabled=true`). There is **no central OTel Collector Deployment** and **no per-node DaemonSet** in this stack:

- **Gateway metrics** — gateway pushes OTLP/gRPC → sidecar's `otlp` receiver on `127.0.0.1:4317` → re-exported via the `prometheus` exporter on `:9188`.
- **Container/node metrics** — Prometheus scrapes kubelet/cAdvisor directly (no OTel involvement).
- **CNPG metrics** — Prometheus scrapes the CNPG instance manager on `:9187` directly.

```
documentdb pod
├─ postgres            (CNPG, /metrics :9187)
├─ documentdb-gateway  (OTLP push → 127.0.0.1:4317)
└─ otel-collector      (OTLP in :4317 / Prom out :9188)
```

## Operator changes (under `operator/`)

- **`internal/otel/base_config.yaml`** — adds an `otlp` receiver bound to `127.0.0.1:4317` (loopback only; gateway and collector share pod netns) and wires it into the `metrics` pipeline alongside the existing `sqlquery` receiver.
- **`cnpg-plugins/sidecar-injector/internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go`** — when injecting the sidecar, also adds OTel env vars to the gateway container:
  - `POD_NAME` (downward API)
  - `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317`
  - `OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED=true` ← required: the gateway gates OTel init off by default and checks this env var
  - `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.instance.id=$(POD_NAME)`

  Injection is **idempotent across CREATE and PATCH** via name-based dedup — without this, repeated reconciles double-append entries and CNPG fails with `Pod is invalid: spec: Forbidden: pod updates may not change fields other than ...`.
- **New** `lifecycle_test.go` covers: all-appended, metrics-enabled-present, preserves-existing, idempotent re-invocation, no-gateway-container.
- `internal/otel/config_test.go` extended for the new `otlp` receiver and pipeline wiring.

## Playground (`documentdb-playground/telemetry/local/`)

One-command deploy: `./scripts/deploy.sh` — Kind cluster + cert-manager + operator (from this branch) + observability stack + DocumentDB HA + traffic generators.

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| 3-instance DocumentDB HA cluster | 1 primary + 2 streaming replicas |
| Per-pod OTel Collector sidecar | Injected by the operator's CNPG plugin |
| Prometheus | Scrapes sidecars (annotation discovery), CNPG, kubelet/cAdvisor |
| Grafana | Two dashboards: Gateway, Internals |
| Traffic generators | RW to primary, RO to replicas, with deliberate error injection |

Dashboards' Instance variable pivots on the `pod` label (set by the collector's `resource` processor) — Prometheus's scrape `instance` label clobbers OTel's `service.instance.id`.

Sidecar Prometheus port is **9188** (not the conventional 9187, which collides with the CNPG instance-manager in the same pod netns).

`validate.sh` polls up to 120s for `db_client_operations_total` and **fails red** if absent — surfaces gateway-image issues clearly instead of warning.

## ⚠️ Gateway image requirement

The default upstream gateway image does **not** yet emit OTLP `db_client_*` metrics — that instrumentation lives in pgmongo and has not been published in an upstream release. The playground's `cluster.yaml` therefore pins:

```yaml
gatewayImage: "udsmiley/documentdb-gateway-otel:k8s-pgmongo-main-latest"
```

Once an upstream release ships with OTel metrics, drop the pin to fall back to the operator default. README §Gateway image documents the build recipe (pgmongo `oss` → emulator-shape image → re-wrap with this repo's `Dockerfile_gateway_public_image` for the K8s slim shape).

## Documentation (`docs/.../monitoring/`)

- **Architecture overview** — sidecar injection flow, operator's `base_config.yaml`, ServiceMonitor examples
- **Metrics reference** — gateway metrics, container resources, CNPG/PostgreSQL metrics, OTel naming conventions
- Updated `mkdocs.yml` navigation

body:
## Summary

- Remove the unauthenticated `GET /api/auth/setup-token` endpoint that exposed the bootstrap token over HTTP, allowing any network client to retrieve it and create the admin account
- Replace with file-based token sharing: the backend writes the token to a file on disk, and the SvelteKit SSR loader reads it directly from the filesystem during server-side rendering
- When the token file is unavailable (e.g., split-host deployments), the frontend falls back to a manual text input where the operator can paste the token from server logs
- Make `bootstrap_token` always required on `POST /api/auth/setup` (remove the conditional skip path)
- Add `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE` env var support for explicit file path configuration
- Align with the existing Docker s6 init pattern which already writes the token to `${CONFIG_DIR}/data/.bootstrap_token`

## Security

This closes a high-severity authentication bypass where an attacker could call `GET /api/auth/setup-token` to retrieve the bootstrap token, then use it with `POST /api/auth/setup` to create the admin account before the legitimate operator. The token now never travels over HTTP.

## Test plan

- [ ] Backend tests pass (`uv run pytest tests/test_admin_setup.py -v` -- 12/12)
- [ ] Frontend tests pass (`bun run test` -- 281/281)
- [ ] dev_cli tests pass (`uv run pytest dev_cli/tests/ -v` -- 31/31)
- [ ] `GET /api/auth/setup-token` returns 404
- [ ] `POST /api/auth/setup` without `bootstrap_token` returns error
- [ ] Docker automation unaffected (s6 script writes same file path)
- [ ] Local dev works via `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE` env var from dev_cli

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes join runtime-filter construction for `LEFT ANTI JOIN`, which is correctness-critical and could affect query results/performance for anti-joins and NULLable keys. Scope is contained to runtime-filter planning plus new stateless regression coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes incorrect results when `enable_join_runtime_filters=1` for multi-key `LEFT ANTI JOIN` by switching from per-column `NOT IN` filters combined with `AND` to a single tuple-based runtime filter (build/apply `tuple(key1, key2, ...)` with inferred common supertypes and casts).
> 
> Adds NULL-safe behavior for ANTI JOIN runtime filters by OR-ing the filter condition with `isNull()` checks for any nullable/LowCardinality-nullable join keys so rows containing NULL keys always bypass the exclusion filter. Adds a comprehensive stateless regression test suite covering multi-key, mixed-type casts, NULL/LowCardinality NULLs, overflow/disabled filter behavior, and non-ANTI joins.

author: xnvargas
body:
## Summary
Fixes three critical issues in the document artifact creation tool that were causing agent failures and context window bloat:

1. **Category enum validation** — Agent was passing invalid category values (e.g., "Documentation", "Technical") that don't exist in the PostgreSQL `document_category` enum. Now validates against actual enum values and falls back to `'agent-artifact'`.

2. **Parameterized SQL queries** — Content containing colons (markdown, JSON, URLs) was being misinterpreted by SQLAlchemy's `text()` as named bind parameters. Switched to `run_query_params()` with explicit parameter binding.

3. **Condensed error messages** — Full SQL statements and content were being echoed back to the agent, filling the context window. Errors are now concise for the agent, with full details only in server logs.

Additionally implements **per-tool retry limiting** in the LangGraph factory to prevent infinite retry loops when tools consistently fail.

## Key Changes

### `src/tools/langchain/swot/relational/create_document_artifact.py`
- Added `VALID_CATEGORIES` frozenset with all PostgreSQL enum values (base + Phase 2.3 expansion)
- Added `_validate_category()` function to normalize and validate category input, falling back to `'agent-artifact'` with logged warning
- Replaced string concatenation SQL with `run_query_params()` calls using named bind parameters (`:doc_id`, `:title`, `:content`, etc.)
- Refactored `execute()` method with clear sections (input validation, MinIO upload, parameterized inserts, entity linking, search mode setup)
- Improved error handling: full exception details logged server-side, condensed message returned to agent
- Updated schema to include `enum` constraint and improved descriptions for category and search_mode fields
- Added logging import and logger instance

### `src/utils/langgraph_factory.py`
- Added `MAX_TOOL_ATTEMPTS` constant (3) to limit consecutive failures per tool
- Added `MAX_ERROR_MSG_CHARS` constant (300) to truncate error messages sent to agent
- Added `_merge_tool_attempts()` reducer function for state merging
- Extended `MessagesState` TypedDict with `tool_attempts: Annotated[Dict[str, int], _merge_tool_attempts]` to track per-tool failure counts
- Enhanced `tool_node()` to:
  - Check retry limit before executing tool (blocks execution if MAX_TOOL_ATTEMPTS reached)
  - Track soft errors (tool returns error string) separately from exceptions
  - Reset failure counter on success
  - Increment failure counter on both exceptions and tool-returned errors
  - Return condensed error messages to agent with attempt count
  - Log full details server-side only
- Updated `llm_call()` to initialize `tool_attempts` in state

### `src/utils/db/sql.py`
- Added `run_query_params()` function for parameterized SQL execution
- Uses SQLAlchemy `text()` with explicit bind parameters to avoid misinterpreting colons in raw content
- Handles both SELECT (returns rows) and DML (returns row count) statements
- Properly commits transactions via engine connection

### `src/utils/db/__init__.py`
- Updated docstring to mention parameterized query helper

## Implementation Details
- Category validation is case-insensitive and strips whitespace
- Search mode validation also uses frozenset for consistency
- Error messages to agent are truncated to MAX_ERROR_MSG_CHARS to prevent context window bloat
- Tool result truncation (MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS = 4000) is preserved for large outputs
- Retry blocking message explicitly instructs agent not to retry and suggests alternatives
- All parameterized queries use `::type` PostgreSQL casts for type safety (e.g., `:doc_id ::uuid`, `:category ::document_category`)

body:
## Summary

All three Endor skills have been rewritten to reduce token usage, eliminate redundant tool calls, and fix incorrect API patterns.

---

### `endor-scan` (170 → 97 lines, -43%)

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Used `--output-type json`, dumping 107 findings into context | Use `--output-type summary` first, then targeted JSON parse for critical/high only |
| No mention of actual JSON structure | Documented that output uses `all_findings` key with `spec`/`meta` sub-keys |
| Duplicated reachability docs (30 lines) | Condensed to 5-line reference |
| Duplicated error handling section | Cut to essentials |
| Language detection as a separate step (Glob calls) | Removed — `endorctl` auto-detects languages |

### `endor-scan-full` (219 → 120 lines, -45%)

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Instructed to save raw JSON to cache (huge files) | Cache only the parsed/classified results |
| Multiple Python passes to discover structure, classify, then re-read | Single Python script does parse + classify + sort + cache + output |
| Instructed to call `get_resource` per finding UUID (N API calls) | Removed — all data is already in the scan output |
| Duplicated reachability docs from `endor-scan` | Condensed reference |
| Stored `raw_results` in cache consuming disk/read tokens | Cache only classified summaries |

### `endor-upgrade-impact` (148 → 88 lines, -41%)

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Project UUID lookup used `meta.name contains 'repo'` which failed (name is a full git URL) | Reuse UUID from prior scan output, or query by known UUID |
| Raw API JSON dumped into context (100+ projects listed) | Pipe through Python to extract only `pkg` |
| Duplicate dedup not handled | Added `seen` set to deduplicate entries |
| Verbose presentation templates | Trimmed to essentials |

---

### Token savings estimate

For a full workflow (scan → full scan → upgrade impact):

- **~60% fewer tool calls** — no structure discovery, no re-parsing, no failed encoding retries
- **~70% less JSON in context** — pipe through Python extractors instead of dumping raw output
- **Project UUID reuse** eliminates the ~6,000-token project list dump
- **Single-pass parsing** eliminates 3–4 redundant Python invocations

author: renjiyuusei
body:
💡 **What:** The optimization implemented is avoiding the repeated instantiation of `Gson` in `MainActivity.kt`. It now uses a single, class-level `private val gson = Gson()` instance for `fetchPreloadedAppsRemote` operations. Additionally, the changelog in `CHANGELOG.md` was updated. 🎯 **Why:** The issue highlighted that creating a `Gson()` instance on every API response call consumes memory and stresses the Garbage Collector unnecessarily. A shared instance prevents this allocation overhead, significantly speeding up the parsing phase. 📊 **Measured Improvement:** - A Java benchmark (`tools/BenchmarkGson.java`) was executed locally processing 10,000 JSON decoding iterations. - Baseline (Repeated Allocation Time): 548.4 ms - Optimized (Shared Instance Time): 66.0 ms - Improvement: The shared instance is approximately **8.3x faster**, reducing computation time and GC pressure noticeably. --- *PR created automatically by Jules for task [10137215803618862772](https://jules.google.com/task/10137215803618862772) started by @RenjiYuusei*

Greptile Summary

PR này tối ưu việc sử dụng `Gson` trong `MainActivity.kt` bằng cách chuyển từ khởi tạo inline `Gson()` mỗi lần gọi sang một instance dùng chung ở cấp class (`private val gson = Gson()`), và cập nhật `CHANGELOG.md` tương ứng. - Thay đổi nhỏ, khu trú tại hàm `fetchPreloadedAppsRemote` — giảm áp lực GC khi nhận API response lặp lại. - `Gson` được ghi nhận là thread-safe cho `fromJson`/`toJson`, nên việc dùng chung instance là an toàn. - Mô tả trong `CHANGELOG.md` dùng cụm "dùng chung" là chính xác với triển khai hiện tại. - Lưu ý: codebase (`Models.kt`) đã có tiền lệ đặt `gson` trong `companion object` — pattern này tốt hơn vì đảm bảo chỉ có một instance duy nhất trong toàn bộ vòng đời ứng dụng, bất kể `MainActivity` bị recreate bao nhiêu lần, nhưng điều này đã được thảo luận trong các luồng review trước.

body:
### WHY are these changes introduced?

Fixes scaffolding tests for npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun that were all failing in CI.

**Root causes:**
1. Node setup was configured with `cache: 'npm'` and `cache-dependency-path: '**/package-lock.json'`
2. The repo only has `pnpm-lock.yaml` (it's a pnpm workspace)
3. Tests tried to run `npm ci` which failed because no `package-lock.json` exists

**Error seen:**
```
##[error]Some specified paths were not resolved, unable to cache dependencies.
npm error The npm ci command can only install with an existing package-lock.json
```

### WHAT is this pull request doing?

Updates the scaffolding tests to use pnpm for monorepo dependency installation, aligning with all other CI jobs.

**Changes:**
1. Added pnpm setup step before node setup
2. Configured node setup to use `cache: 'pnpm'` with `cache-dependency-path: 'pnpm-lock.yaml'`
3. Changed `npm ci` → `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
4. Changed `npm run build:pkg` → `pnpm run build:pkg`

**Why this is correct:**
- All other CI jobs (lint, typecheck, unit tests, E2E tests) use pnpm for monorepo deps
- The scaffolding tests still test all 4 package managers (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun) as intended
- They just use pnpm to install the monorepo's dependencies before running the actual scaffolding tests
- The scaffolded test projects use their respective package managers (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun)

### HOW to test your changes?

**Tested locally:**
1. Built packages: `pnpm install && pnpm run build:pkg`
2. Scaffolded test project with npm:
   ```bash

     --no-git \

     --routes \
     --markets none \
     --styling none
   ```
3. Verified:
   - ✅ `package-lock.json` created
   - ✅ `npm run build` succeeds

**Verify in CI:**
- Wait for CI to pass on this PR
- All 4 scaffolding tests (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun) should pass

regular admins see only their own - Removed CREATE from always-blocked list (it now routes through approval queue) - Still blocked: DROP · TRUNCATE · ALTER · GRANT · REVOKE · EXECUTE · xp_* · sp_* - `frontend/app/api/admin/sql/[id]/route.ts` - Approve / Reject now gated by ADMIN_MASTER_EMAIL instead of super_admin role - Only the master admin email can execute or reject queued requests - Cancel (DELETE) still available for the original submitter - `frontend/app/api/admin/sql/execute/route.ts` (new) - Handles direct query execution for the editor's Run Query flow - Non-master admins: SELECT-family queries only - Master admin with masterOverride: true: any validated query - Always-blocked patterns enforced before any execution - Returns up to 500 rows capped in the response #### Navigation (unchanged from previous PR, kept working) - AdminNavbar: SQL nav item with Terminal icon - AdminFooter: SQL Terminal quick link - Admin Database page: SQL Terminal button in header --- ### Security Controls | Operation | Regular Admin | Master Admin (ADMIN_MASTER_EMAIL) | |---------------------|---------------------|-----------------------------------| | SELECT / EXPLAIN | Direct execution | Direct execution | | INSERT / UPDATE | Submit for approval | Direct OR approve own submission | | DELETE / CREATE | Submit for approval | Direct OR approve own submission | | DROP / TRUNCATE | Blocked | Blocked | | ALTER / GRANT | Blocked | Blocked | | Approve requests | Not allowed | Allowed | | Reject requests | Not allowed | Allowed | | View all requests | Own only | All requests | - Comment injection bypass prevented: -- and /* */ comments stripped before pattern matching - All executions and approvals logged in the `sql_command_requests` audit table - Execution results capped at 500 rows server-side; UI shows max 200 rows --- ### Environment Variable Required ``` ADMIN_MASTER_EMAIL=your-master-admin@email.com ``` This email (and only this email) can approve/reject SQL requests and run write queries directly. author: realkai42
body:
## Problem

When many channels or plugins each carry large `configSchema` objects (e.g. 16+ Feishu channels), `buildMergedSchemaCacheKey` concatenates all of them into a single JSON string via `JSON.stringify({ plugins, channels })`.  With enough entries or large enough schemas this string can exceed the engine's string-length limit and throws:

```
RangeError: Invalid string length
```

Fixes #36508.

## Solution

Replace the single large `JSON.stringify` with per-item djb2 hashing. Each plugin/channel's schema and hints are hashed independently into a 32-bit integer, and only the compact IDs + hash values are joined into the cache key string. This bounds the cache key size to `O(N)` in the number of entries regardless of individual schema sizes.

## Changes

- `src/config/schema.ts`: add `hashSchemaItem(value)` (djb2 hash), rewrite `buildMergedSchemaCacheKey` to use per-item hashes instead of full serialization
- `src/config/schema.test.ts`: add two new tests:
  - "does not cache-collide when same plugin ID has different schemas"
  - "handles many channels without RangeError" (20 channels × 50 fields each)
- `CHANGELOG.md`: document the fix

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run src/config/schema.test.ts` — 12/12 tests pass
- [x] Existing "caches merged schemas for identical plugin/channel metadata" test still passes (same input → same cached result)
- [x] New collision-safety test: two plugins with the same ID but different schemas produce distinct cache keys
- [x] New stress test: 20 channels with 50 properties each completes without `RangeError`

body:
Updates the buoyancy simulation and scene setup for the 25x50 pool environment. The changes improve the realism of buoyancy calculations by using the AUV's actual volume and water density.

**Buoyancy Physics Improvements**
* Refactored the `Buoyancy` script (`Buoyancy.cs`) to calculate buoyancy force using Archimedes' principle: buoyancy is now based on the AUV's actual volume (approximated by box colliders) and water density, rather than a fixed force value. This improves physical accuracy.
* Added references to `WaterSurface` and `HydrodynamicDrag` components for projecting buoyancy points and accessing water density, respectively. The buoyancy force is now only applied when the AUV is submerged, and debug logging is available. 
* Enabled `scriptInteractions` in `Pool Water` Game Object. **This is what allows the buoyancy to determine if the AUV is underwater by determining if center of buoyancy is under the water surface**
* When `Pool Water` HDRP render is deactivated via the `NoWaterMode` setting ("Enable Water" option turned off), surface is instead assumed to be the surface's transfom position.

body:
### What:
Added comprehensive mechanical profiling to the `Datamine` class in `lib/datalib.py`. The tool now automatically identifies and categorizes cards based on:
- **Structural Mechanics:** Activated abilities (via `:`), Triggered abilities (line starts), ETB effects, Modal/Choice structures (via delimiters), and X-costs/effects.
- **Keyword Abilities:** Common keywords like Flying, Trample, Lifelink, Ward, Scry, Token creation, and more.

The analysis is recursive, ensuring split and double-faced cards are fully profiled. The `summarize.py` CLI utility now includes a "Mechanical Breakdown" section with frequencies and bar charts. Profiling data is also included in JSON exports for downstream analysis.

### Why:
I noticed that while the existing tools provided excellent analysis of card metadata (colors, CMC, rarities), they lacked insight into the actual gameplay mechanics contained within the text. For users training AI models, understanding the mechanical distribution of their training set—and the mechanical coherence of generated output—is crucial. This feature fills that gap by providing a high-level "mechanical fingerprint" of any card collection or generated dataset without requiring manual labeling.

author: danielvegamyhre
body:
This [twitter post ](https://x.com/PV90169/status/2027746935843832044?s=20) claimed B200 memory bandwidth is actually 7680gbps, not 8192gbps, as the original bitwidth of the memory bus reported by CUDA drivers has been updated/corrected from 8192 bits to 7680 bits.

I confirmed this claim using Claude to write a simple CUDA C++ file to query the device driver:

```
=== Device 0: NVIDIA B200 ===
Memory Bus Width: 7680 bits
Total Global Memory: 178.35 GB
L2 Cache Size: 126.50 MB
Compute Capability: 10.0
Number of SMs: 148
Warp Size: 32
Max Threads per Block: 1024
Max Threads per SM: 2048
Shared Memory per Block: 48.00 KB
Shared Memory per SM: 228.00 KB
Registers per Block: 65536
Registers per SM: 65536
ECC Enabled: Yes
```

And nvidia-smi to get the memory clock frequency:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.mem,clocks.max.mem --format=csv

clocks.current.memory [MHz], clocks.max.memory [MHz]
3996 MHz, 3996 MHz
```
Bandwidth = (7680bits/8bits per byte)*(3996 MHz memory clock) * 2 DDR / 1e12 = 7.672 TB/s

This PR updates our benchmark/roofline utils accordingly.

author: romankolosok
body:
This pull request introduces major improvements to both the CI/CD pipeline and the Avalonia application setup. The Jenkins pipeline has been modernized for cross-platform builds and automated GitHub releases, while the application has been migrated from WPF to Avalonia, including new XAML-based styling and updated service registrations. These changes enhance build reliability, deployment automation, and UI consistency across platforms.

**Jenkins Pipeline Modernization**

* The pipeline now builds and publishes self-contained Linux and Windows app packages for main/master branches, and automates GitHub releases with attached platform-specific archives, replacing the previous Windows-only release logic.
* The build stage now compiles the full solution (`PasswordManager.sln`) instead of just the core and tests, improving cross-platform compatibility.
* The Supabase integration test setup is more robust: it stops any previous stack, starts fresh, and resets the DB schema with error tolerance, ensuring cleaner CI runs.

**Avalonia Migration and UI Styling**

* The application has been migrated from WPF to Avalonia, with the main app XAML now in `App.axaml`, introducing a comprehensive set of styles for inputs, buttons, and controls for a consistent, modern UI.
* The startup logic is refactored for Avalonia: initialization now uses `Initialize()` and `OnFrameworkInitializationCompleted()` instead of WPF's `OnStartup`, and the clipboard service is switched to `AvaloniaClipboardService`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ebf81ec9bfa30f78b539771150481622835c1d8c2b5975aceefdce374ebe2374R1-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ebf81ec9bfa30f78b539771150481622835c1d8c2b5975aceefdce374ebe2374L10-L29) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ebf81ec9bfa30f78b539771150481622835c1d8c2b5975aceefdce374ebe2374L85-L91)
* Service registration is updated for Avalonia, including support for dialogs and correct shutdown behavior for desktop apps.

These changes collectively improve platform support, deployment automation, and user experience.

body:
### Motivation
- Replace hardcoded, machine-specific paths with portable CLI arguments to make case generation and execution reusable across environments.
- Improve robustness of CSV mutations so missing rows/columns or type mismatches do not cause crashes during bulk case generation.
- Make the execution workflow more resilient by normalizing and centralizing logging and providing options to skip or force reruns.

### Description
- Converted `data/EEM26/EEM26_create_cases_v2.py` into a CLI script with `--base-dir`, `--cases-dir`, and `--clean` options and implemented in-memory caching of source CSV bytes to avoid repeated disk reads.
- Centralized CSV mutation logic in `modify_csv` and added a defensive helper `_safe_loc_set` to guard writes when rows/columns are absent, plus portable `read_and_set_index` handling and robust `Duration` assignment; files are written with `df.to_csv` after safe updates.
- Converted `data/EEM26/EEM26_execute_cases_v2.py` into a CLI workflow with `--base-dir`, `--cases-dir`, `--log-file`, `--src-dir`, `--solver`, `--force-rerun`, and other flags, and implemented `initialize_log`/`write_log` helpers to normalize log columns and atomically update the execution CSV.
- Added safer objective extraction in `_safe_objective`, dynamic `src` import path handling, and preserved the previous success-skip semantics while enabling a `--force-rerun` override.

### Testing
- Compiled both scripts with `python -m py_compile data/EEM26/EEM26_create_cases_v2.py data/EEM26/EEM26_execute_cases_v2.py`, which succeeded.
- Verified CLI help output for both scripts with `python data/EEM26/EEM26_create_cases_v2.py --help` and `python data/EEM26/EEM26_execute_cases_v2.py --help`, which printed expected usage text.
- No runtime model executions were performed as part of this PR; the execution script was validated for import/CLI behavior only.

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive skill documentation for TableTest and Spec-by-Example, including reference guides, evaluation benchmarks, and skill definitions across two iterations of development.

## Key Changes

### Skill Definitions
- **tabletest/SKILL.md**: Updated with expanded trigger conditions and clearer guidance on when to use TableTest
- **spec-by-example/SKILL.md**: Updated description to clarify trigger conditions for vague requirements and conditional logic

### Reference Documentation (TableTest)
Added 11 reference guides covering:
- **common-patterns.md**: Consolidating identity + status, handling positional outputs
- **column-design.md**: When to split vs. combine columns, evolving design iteratively
- **type-converters.md**: Built-in conversions and custom converter patterns
- **async-and-performance.md**: Testing non-blocking execution and performance behavior
- **table-design-advanced.md**: Orthogonal concerns and avoiding cross-multiplication
- **example-patterns.md**: Business rules, validation, and state transition examples
- **incremental-development.md**: Iterative TableTest development workflow
- **dependency-setup.md**: Correct Maven/Gradle coordinates for TableTest
- **value-sets.md**: Using `{...}` syntax for multiple input examples
- **large-tables.md**: Comments, grouping, and external file organization
- **consolidating-tests.md**: Removing redundant individual tests after building comprehensive tables
- **provided-parameters.md**: Using JUnit-provided parameters like `@TempDir`
- **pair-programming.md**: Collaborative cadence for writing TableTests
- **testing-reveals-bugs.md**: How test design can surface implementation issues

### Evaluation Framework
- **evals.json**: 6 evaluation scenarios covering conversion, parsing, dependency setup, loan approval, order transitions, and discount interactions
- **Iteration 1 & 2 benchmarks**: Detailed performance metrics comparing "with_skill" vs "old_skill" configurations across all evaluations
- **Evaluation outputs**: Grading rubrics, timing data, and sample outputs for each scenario

### Evaluation Review Pages
- **iteration-1/eval-review.html**: Interactive HTML dashboard for Iteration 1 results
- **iteration-2/eval-review.html**: Interactive HTML dashboard for Iteration 2 results with tabbed interface for benchmark comparison

### Utility Scripts
- **format-table.sh**: Bash script for formatting TableTest tables using the tabletest-formatter CLI

### Workspace Organization
Documentation is duplicated across two workspace structures:
- `skills-workspace/iteration-1/` and `skills-workspace/iteration-2/` for iteration-specific snapshots
- `skills-workspace/skill-snapshot-tabletest/` and `skills-workspace/skill-snapshot-spec-by-example/` for consolidated skill snapshots

## Notable Implementation Details

- Reference guides use real-world examples with clear "do this" vs "don't do this" patterns
- Evaluation framework includes both positive and negative test cases to validate skill effectiveness
- HTML dashboards provide visual comparison of skill performance across iterations

## Problem

author: lucos-architect[bot]
body:
Closes #30

## Summary

Adds ADR-0002 documenting the agreed design for how audit-raised issues interact with GitHub's auto-close behaviour.

### Key decisions

- **Audit result is source of truth**, not issue state
- **Convention passes:** do nothing (no "now passing" comments)
- **Convention fails, open issue exists:** do nothing
- **Convention fails, no open issue:** create a new issue (never reopen old ones)
- **`audit-finding` label** on all audit-raised issues for identification
- **No suppression mechanism** -- if a convention does not apply, update the convention logic itself
- **Auto-close is fine** -- the system self-heals on the next sweep if a fix was incomplete

### Changes to existing issues

Posted a comment on #28 (Raise GitHub issues for failing conventions) removing the "comment when passing" requirement, which this ADR supersedes.

author: joshuaseidel
body:
## Summary
- Adds real-time baby monitoring AI using the RK3566's built-in NPU (0.8-1.0 TOPS)
- YOLOv8n INT8 model runs at ~1 fps in a dedicated inference thread, independent of the 30fps video pipeline
- Detects: baby present/absent, awake/sleeping, face covered, distress (high motion)
- Frame differencing for motion detection works even without the RKNN model

## New files
- `radxa/compositor/src/baby_ai.h` — public API (init, feed_frame, get_status, enable/disable)
- `radxa/compositor/src/baby_ai.c` — RKNN inference, NV12→RGB conversion, motion detection, state machine

## Modified files
- `main.c` — AI init/start/destroy lifecycle, feed camera frames to AI
- `control_channel.c/h` — `AI on`/`AI off`/`AI status` commands, AI state in STATUS JSON
- `overlay.c` — Color-coded status indicator (green=awake, blue=sleeping, red=alert, grey=absent)

## Architecture
```
Camera NV12 frame → baby_ai_feed_frame() → [copy to double buffer]
                                                    ↓
                                          inference_thread (1 fps)
                                                    ↓
                                          NV12 → RGB resize → NPU
                                                    ↓
                                          YOLOv8n detection + motion
                                                    ↓
                                          baby_ai_status_t (thread-safe)
                                                    ↓
                              overlay reads status → color indicator on screen
                              control channel → JSON in STATUS response
```

## Build notes
- Requires `librknnrt.so` and `rknn_api.h` from [rknn-toolkit2](https://github.com/rockchip-linux/rknn-toolkit2)
- Define `BABY_AI_STUB` to compile without RKNN SDK (motion detection still works)
- Model file: `yolov8n.rknn` at `/opt/aadongle/models/baby_detect.rknn`

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify compiles with `BABY_AI_STUB` on macOS/x86 (no RKNN)
- [ ] Verify compiles with RKNN SDK on Radxa (aarch64)
- [ ] Test `AI on`/`AI off`/`AI status` via control channel
- [ ] Verify STATUS JSON includes `baby_state` and `motion` fields
- [ ] Verify overlay indicator renders in correct position and color
- [ ] Benchmark NPU inference time on RK3566 (<100ms target)
- [ ] Test motion detection without model loaded

body:
The [Opquast Digital Quality Checklist](https://checklists.opquast.com/en/digital-quality/) (v5, 2025–2030, 245 rules, CC BY-SA 4.0) covers accessibility, security, performance, privacy, ecodesign, and web quality — but had no representation in this repo's `examples/` guidance layer.

## New file: `examples/OPQUAST_DIGITAL_QUALITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md`

765-line AI-actionable guide translating all 245 rules into concrete implementation requirements across 14 sections:

| Section | Highlights |
|---|---|
| Forms | `aria-required`/`aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`, correct `input type`, password reveal, multi-step flow |
| Security | HTTPS + HSTS, CSP, SRI, `X-Content-Type-Options`, DMARC/SPF |
| Presentation | Contrast ratios, no blocked zoom, `text-transform` over uppercase HTML, print styles |
| Navigation | Skip links, no `outline: none`, logical tab order, modal close button patterns |
| Structure/Code | UTF-8, unique IDs, no `<meta http-equiv="refresh">`, tagged PDFs, scoped table headers |
| Internationalisation | `lang` on `<html>` and inline spans, `hreflang`, international dialling codes |

Also includes:
- **AI summary table** — one-line enforceable rule per category for quick agent scanning
- **WCAG 2.2 mapping** — cross-references Opquast rule numbers to WCAG success criteria (e.g., rules 116–118 → SC 1.1.1, rule 193 → SC 1.4.4)
- Consistent back-links to [opquast.com](https://www.opquast.com/) and both EN/FR checklist URLs per CC BY-SA attribution requirements

## Supporting changes

- **`examples/TRUSTED_SOURCES.yaml`** — two new entries: `opquast` (opquast.com) and `opquast-checklist` (checklists.opquast.com), `license: CC-BY-SA-4.0`, `ai_scraping: allowed`

author: lakshya-chourasia
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced CSS `@import` for Google Fonts with HTML `<link>` tags, combined all font families into a single request, and added `<link rel="preconnect">` hints.

🎯 **Why**: CSS `@import` blocks parallel downloading because the browser must download and parse the CSS file before discovering the font requests. Moving fonts to `<link>` tags in the HTML `<head>` eliminates this request chain, and preconnecting establishes early connections to the font origins.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces critical rendering path latency. The browser can now discover and download fonts earlier, resulting in faster First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).

🔬 **Measurement**: Verify by inspecting the "Network" tab in DevTools. The font stylesheet request (`fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...`) will now start in parallel with `css/style.css`, rather than waiting for `style.css` to finish downloading. Additionally, the preconnects will show early DNS/TCP/TLS resolution for the font domains.

## Summary
- Corrected the `ParticleFrameCallback__5CGameFiiiiiP3Vec` declaration to include its final `Vec*` parameter.
- Updated `pppFrameCallBackDistance` to pass the world-space callback position (`&local_28`) and use the `Game` base pointer form that matches existing call-site codegen patterns.

## Units/functions improved
- Unit: `main/pppCallBackDistance`
- Function: `pppFrameCallBackDistance`

## Progress evidence
- `ninja` global progress before this change:
  - Code: `259852 / 1855300` bytes (`2061 / 4733` functions)
- `ninja` global progress after this change:
  - Code: `260124 / 1855300` bytes (`2062 / 4733` functions)
- Net: `+272` matched code bytes and `+1` matched function.
- Unit report now shows all functions in `main/pppCallBackDistance` at `fuzzy_match_percent: 100.0`.

## Plausibility rationale
- The symbol name `ParticleFrameCallback__5CGameFiiiiiP3Vec` explicitly encodes a trailing `P3Vec` argument, so declaring and passing a `Vec*` is source-plausible and ABI-consistent.
- The callback already prepares `local_28` in world space via `PSMTXMultVec`; passing it to the callback aligns with intended behavior rather than compiler coaxing.

body:
…e_company

Problema:
El wizard change_company presentaba tiempos inaceptables en facturas con muchas líneas. Con un profiler de Speedscope sobre una factura de 80 líneas se midieron ~14 segundos, de los cuales:

- 10.47s (75%) en _compute_account_id: cada asignación individual de account_id en una línea disparaba _sync_dynamic_lines del move (recálculo completo de impuestos, payment terms, totales y balances), repitiendo la sincronización N veces (una por línea).
- 1.65s (12%) en invoice_line_ids.tax_ids = False: la limpieza de impuestos también disparaba sincronización línea por línea.
- 1.13s (8%) en la reasignación de tax_ids por línea dentro de _get_change_company_line_taxes: el doble for (líneas × impuestos) ejecutaba un search() a la DB por cada impuesto de cada línea (~1200-1800 queries) y luego hacía un write individual por línea.

Solución (3 optimizaciones):

1) skip_invoice_sync global + sincronización final única:
   Se crea move = self.move_id.with_context(skip_invoice_sync=True)
   y se usa para TODAS las operaciones sobre líneas (cuentas, impuestos,
   payment terms, etc.). Esto evita que _sync_dynamic_lines se ejecute
   en cada asignación individual. Al final, se fuerza una única
   sincronización usando el context manager _sync_dynamic_lines sobre
   self.move_id (sin skip_invoice_sync), replicando el patrón que usa
   write() internamente en Odoo 18.
   Impacto estimado: de ~10.5s a ~0.15s para _compute_account_id.

2) _get_change_company_line_taxes con mapping + agrupación en lote:
   - Se recolectan los tax IDs únicos de todas las líneas (típicamente 3-5 impuestos distintos en vez de 1200+ repeticiones).
   - Se busca el equivalente en la nueva compañía UNA sola vez por impuesto único y se guarda en un dict tax_mapping.
   - Se agrupan las líneas por su combinación original de impuestos (defaultdict) y se hace UN solo write de tax_ids por grupo. Impacto: de ~1800 queries + 600 writes a ~5 searches + ~5 writes.

3) Optimización de original_taxes (backup de impuestos):
   - fp_tax_groups pasa de ser un recordset (comparación O(n) con 'not in') a un set de IDs (lookup O(1)).
   - Se reemplaza .filtered(lambda).ids por una list comprehension directa sin crear recordsets intermedios.
   - without_product se asigna en lote con un solo write en vez de iterar línea por línea.

author: ain-soph
body:
When using `Dataset.map()` with `num_proc > 1`, shards containing only empty lists get their features inferred as `List(Value('null'))`, which is incompatible with `List(Struct({...}))` from shards with actual data.

The existing `_check_if_features_can_be_aligned` and `_align_features` only handled top-level `Value('null')` compatibility. This commit adds a `_is_null_feature()` helper that recursively checks for null types inside container features (`List, LargeList, Sequence`), and uses it in both alignment functions.

Fixes #8046

### Motivation

body:
### Motivation
- Garantir que, ao selecionar um tipo de pagamento que seja cartão de crédito ou cheque, as parcelas seguintes assumam o mesmo tipo para consistência operacional. 
- Tratar variações com acentos (ex.: "Crédito") para que a detecção seja robusta usando normalização de texto.

### Description
- Atualiza o listener `parcelasBody.addEventListener('input', ...)` em `vendas/nova.php` no bloco `if (event.target.classList.contains('parcela-tipo'))` para normalizar o valor selecionado com `normalize('NFD')`, remover acentos e aplicar `toLowerCase()`.
- Quando o texto normalizado contém `credito` ou `cheque`, aplica o mesmo `tipoPagamento` a todas as parcelas de `idx + 1` até o final do array `parcelas` e chama `renderParcelas()` para atualizar a tabela visualmente.
- Mantém o comportamento atual para outros tipos (ex.: `PIX`, `Dinheiro`) e preserva o fluxo existente de adicionar/remover parcelas via `contextmenu` e `recalcularParcelas()`.

### Testing
- Executado um snippet Node.js que simulou 4 parcelas e ao definir `Crédito Stone` na parcela 2 a propagação para parcela 3 e 4 ocorreu com sucesso (teste automatizado, passou).

release notes 
# Kubeshark release v53.1.0 (03-05-2026)

**Release is NOT ready yet!** - DO NOT USE

## Release Highlights

Kubeshark 53.1.0 introduces comprehensive L4 (TCP/UDP) network flow visibility with real-time connectivity tracking, handshake latency percentiles, and a new cluster-wide L4 map in the UI.

The release adds a built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, enabling AI-powered network analysis through standardized tool integrations including snapshot management, L4/L7 querying, and PCAP export.

Snapshot workflows have been significantly enhanced with cloud storage support, delayed dissection capabilities, and streamlined download/upload operations.

Several critical CVEs have been patched, build security has been hardened following a responsibly-disclosed token exposure incident, and memory stability improvements have been made throughout the stack.

## New Features

- Add MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for AI-powered network traffic analysis [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/mcp)
- Add MCP tools for querying L4 flows, L7 API calls, snapshot management, and PCAP export [L4 tools](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/mcp/l4_tools) | [L7 tools](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/mcp/l7_tools) | [raw capture tools](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/mcp/raw_capture_tools)
- Add MCP Registry support for official registry submission and discovery
- Add L4 (TCP/UDP) real-time network flow visibility with connection tracking [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/l4_to_l7)
- Add cluster-wide L4 connectivity map in the dashboard [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/service_map)
- Add P50/P90/P99 TCP handshake latency percentiles for network health monitoring [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/mcp/tcp_insights)
- Add snapshot cloud storage support (AWS S3 with cross-account IAM role assumption, Azure Blob) [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/traffic_snapshots)
- Add snapshot download and upload via HTTP REST endpoints
- Add delayed dissection mode for post-capture L7 protocol analysis [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/l7_api_delayed)
- Add automatic dissection trigger after snapshot completion [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/mcp/delayed_dissection)
- Add KFL2 query language with GraphQL support for advanced traffic filtering [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/kfl2)
- Add L4 flow and connection entries in the UI with PCAP content loading [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/l4_to_l7)
- Add DNS resolution name as fallback display in traffic entries
- Add --release-helmChartPath CLI flag for deploying with a local Helm chart
- Add captureSelf flag to enable or disable capturing Kubeshark's own traffic
- Add configurable cloud API URL

## Improvements

- Rename flow terminology for consistency (flow for L4, conn for connections)
- Set default TCP and UDP flow timeouts to 20 minutes
- Adjust nginx configuration to support large snapshot uploads and downloads
- Improve L4 to L7 entry relationship tracking and consistency
- Apply DNS resolution as fallback when syscall-based resolution fails
- Optimize UI Docker builds and production bundle loading
- Improve license validation and UI stability for non-enterprise users
- Extend community license grace capacity on node and pod limit overflow
- Allow Pro plans to use license keys without requiring cloud login
- Exclude worker pods from scheduling on nodes that are not ready
- Improve dissection badge UX with updated text and color indicators
- Auto-align selected snapshot nodes with available ones in the UI
- Stop raw packet capture during snapshot download to ensure data consistency [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/traffic_snapshots)
- Batch mode processing for delayed dissection workloads [docs](https://docs.kubeshark.com/en/v2/l7_api_delayed)
- Optimize memory usage in packet capture pipeline

## Bug Fixes

- Fix memory leak in TCP handshake health aggregation
- Fix nil pointer dereferences in MCP L4 flow functions
- Fix crash when storing entries with TCP and UDP connection objects
- Fix L4 flows delayed dissection and PCAP generation
- Fix inter-node flow aggregation in the flows API
- Fix cleanup timings that could cause queries for already-deleted entries
- Fix peer resolution and resolution status population
- Fix frontend resolution display issues
- Fix node view rendering in the workload map
- Fix callback dependency for fetching selected entries in the UI
- Fix handling of empty payload and empty L4 metrics in delayed-dissection entries
- Fix data volume mount placement in Helm chart TLS configuration
- Fix MCP Hub API tool call field naming
- Fix ARM architecture build

## Security

- Harden container build pipeline following a responsibly-disclosed GitHub token exposure in a container image — removed embedded tokens, switched to GitHub App tokens with minimal scopes, improved build isolation
- Fix CVE-2025-30204 by updating golang-jwt to patched versions
- Fix CVE-2025-47914 and CVE-2025-58181 by updating golang.org/x/crypto to 0.45.0
- Add backend license validation for cloud-connected deployments

author: mertselimb
body:
## Summary

Fixes two Android bugs in `handleShareIntent` / `getFileInfo`:

### Bug 1: SecurityException on shared files (fixes #175)

`getFileInfo` calls `resolver.query(uri)` directly on the content URI. On Android 12+, content providers like Google Photos (`MediaContentProvider`) and Downloads (`DownloadStorageProvider`) are not exported. The temporary URI permission granted by `FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION` can expire before the async `getShareIntent` call reaches the native module, causing:

```
java.lang.SecurityException: Permission Denial: opening provider
com.google.android.apps.photos.contentprovider.impl.MediaContentProvider
... that is not exported from UID 10170
```

**Fix:** Copy the file to app cache via `openInputStream` immediately (while URI permission is valid), then read metadata from the local copy. Metadata query and MIME type resolution are wrapped in try-catch so a single provider failure doesn't crash the entire share flow.

### Bug 2: Files with `text/*` MIME types silently dropped

`handleShareIntent` checks `intent.type.startsWith("text/plain")` before checking for `EXTRA_STREAM`. When a file with a `text/*` MIME type (`.txt`, `.csv`, `.html`, etc.) is shared from a file manager, the MIME type is `text/plain` (or another `text/*` variant) but the file is delivered via `EXTRA_STREAM` (not `EXTRA_TEXT`). The code enters the text branch, reads `EXTRA_TEXT` (null), and the share is silently lost.

**Fix:** Check for `EXTRA_STREAM` first in `ACTION_SEND`. If a stream URI exists, always treat it as a file regardless of MIME type. Text handling is only used when there is no stream attachment.

## Testing

Tested with:
- Share image from Google Photos → ✅ file received (was SecurityException)
- Share PDF from Downloads → ✅ file received (was SecurityException)
- Share .txt file from file manager → ✅ file received (was silently dropped)
- Share plain text from browser → ✅ text received (unchanged)
- Share multiple images → ✅ files received (unchanged)

author: dancuo-lohan
body:
## PR Title
Security hardening, SOLID/DRY refactors, and reliability improvements across core framework

## Summary
This PR consolidates a full framework audit pass (plus follow-up passes) and applies fixes across security, performance, SOLID/DRY design, tests, and docs.

Main goals:
- Remove high-risk security gaps (path traversal, proxy trust, unsafe globals, weak request handling)
- Improve architecture (dependency inversion + deduplication)
- Reduce runtime fragility and shell dependence
- Align tests/docs with hardened behavior

## What Changed

### Security fixes
- Escaped image HTML attributes to prevent XSS.
- Hardened HTTPS detection with trusted-proxy support.
- Hardened image path handling to reject traversal and unsafe paths.
- Removed CSRF middleware fallback to global `$_POST`; now request-scoped extraction only.
- Guarded API request-size middleware against seek/tell stream failures.
- Hardened SQL identifier quoting:
  - Reject empty/invalid identifier segments.
  - Properly support dotted identifiers.
- Sanitized updater backup scopes to block traversal and out-of-scope writes.

### SOLID / DRY refactors
- Injected controller factories in handlers (improves DIP/testability).
- Deduplicated action visibility checks via shared inspector.
- Centralized safe relative-path normalization.
- Extracted not-found handler factory from front controller.
- Removed remaining global requested-view state coupling.

### Performance / reliability
- Made controller cache writes atomic/safer.
- Cached timezone identifier lookups.
- Replaced shell-based CPU core detection with safe PHP-only paths.
- Added zero/edge guards in benchmark math.

### API behavior hardening
- Enforced valid JSON payload behavior for API responses.
- Updated API text response docs accordingly.

### Docs and tests
- Added and updated regression tests for all new hardening paths:
  - image traversal
  - CSRF body parsing/global fallback removal
  - API stream edge handling
  - SQL identifier edge cases
  - updater backup-scope traversal
- Documentation updates:
  - CSRF default API behavior
  - trusted proxy configuration (`TRUSTED_PROXIES`)
  - API response behavior notes

## Validation
- Full test suite passes:
  - `OK (142 tests, 302 assertions)`

## Notes for reviewers
- No destructive migrations required.
- Behavior is stricter by design in security-sensitive areas (invalid/traversal paths and malformed identifiers now fail fast).
- Proxy deployments should verify `TRUSTED_PROXIES` is configured correctly.

author: peytonr18
body:
## Summary

Extracts KVP into a standalone crate, `libazureinit-kvp`, and replaces the legacy `libazureinit::kvp` module with a layered, trait-generic architecture.

This keeps azure-init's tracing-based KVP emission behavior while making KVP reusable for external distros without pulling in the full azure-init stack.

- Replaces `libazureinit/src/kvp.rs` (902 lines) with a new workspace crate: `libazureinit-kvp`.
- Moves KVP from async channel/background writer semantics to synchronous `flock`-guarded I/O.
- Preserves existing tracing integration in azure-init while simplifying runtime lifecycle management.
- Adds architecture and API documentation for internal and external consumers.

## What Changed

### New crate: `libazureinit-kvp`

Introduces a 4-layer design plus top-level client wiring:

- **Layer 0:** `KvpStore` trait
  - `HyperVKvpStore` (production pool-file implementation)
  - `InMemoryKvpStore` (test double)
- **Layer 1:** `DiagnosticsKvp<S>`
  - typed diagnostics
  - Azure 1022-byte value chunking support
- **Layer 2:** `TracingKvpLayer<S>`
  - `tracing_subscriber::Layer` adapter
  - handles tracing events/spans and `health_report` passthrough
- **Layer 3:** `ProvisioningReport`
  - typed accessor for `PROVISIONING_REPORT`
- **Top-level:** `Kvp<S>` client to wire all layers together

### Legacy module removed

- Deletes `libazureinit/src/kvp.rs`; functionality now lives in `libazureinit-kvp`.

### `libazureinit` integration simplified

- `libazureinit/src/logging.rs`
  - removes old KVP wrapper/lifecycle plumbing (`JoinHandle`, `CancellationToken`, `halt()`, `close()`)
  - `setup_layers` now returns only `Box<dyn Subscriber + Send + Sync>`
- `src/main.rs`
  - removes KVP shutdown orchestration block
  - no explicit async KVP lifecycle handling needed

### Dependency updates

- `libazureinit` drops direct `fs2`/`sysinfo` usage for KVP internals
- adds path dependency on `libazureinit-kvp`
- workspace now includes `libazureinit-kvp`

### Docs

- Adds `doc/kvp_design.md` (design rationale + architecture)
- Rewrites `doc/libazurekvp.md` (API/reference)
- Aligns docs with implemented key format and `ProvisioningReport` API
- Documents/reporting behavior for long `health_report` values

## Why

- **External reuse:** other distros can consume KVP directly with minimal dependencies.
- **Separation of concerns:** storage, diagnostics, tracing adapter, and provisioning report logic are decoupled.
- **Simpler lifecycle:** no channel draining, shutdown tokens, or background writer task ownership.
- **Testability:** each layer can be tested independently; in-memory testing is straightforward.

## Behavioral Notes

- KVP writes are now synchronous (`flock` + write + unlock) rather than buffered async channel writes.
- Long diagnostic/report values are chunked to account for Azure's read limits.
- `health_report` to `PROVISIONING_REPORT` path preserves long values through chunked writes.

## Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Kvp<S> (top-level client, wires layers)         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 3: ProvisioningReport                     │
│          Typed accessor for PROVISIONING_REPORT │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 2: TracingKvpLayer<S>                     │
│          tracing_subscriber::Layer adapter      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 1: DiagnosticsKvp<S>                      │
│          Typed diagnostic events + chunking     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 0: KvpStore trait                         │
│   ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────┐│
│   │ HyperVKvpStore   │   │ InMemoryKvpStore    ││
│   │ (production)     │   │ (test double)       ││
│   └──────────────────┘   └─────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
See `doc/kvp_design.md` for design rationale and `doc/libazurekvp.md` for API details.

Fixes #239. Supersedes #286.

author: joshuajbouw
body:
## Summary
This PR completes the architectural migration of the CLI frontend, officially detaching the `astrid-cli` binary from the monolithic runtime and establishing it as a pure Unix Socket client that talks to the background `astrid daemon`.

* **Decoupled Architecture**: Ripped out the hardcoded Kernel runtime from the CLI binary. The CLI is now a true "dumb" frontend client that connects to the OS Unix Socket via the `astrid-capsule-cli` WASM proxy. 
* **Autonomous Master Daemon**: The Kernel now boots as a detached background daemon (`astrid daemon`) with an idle monitor, allowing autonomous agents to continue executing even if the user closes their terminal.
* **Async WASM Proxy Bridge**: Implemented a thread-safe `block_on` bridge at the Extism host function boundary (`crates/astrid-capsule/src/engine/wasm/host/net.rs`), allowing the `astrid-capsule-cli.wasm` plugin to natively act as a long-running global proxy socket without deadlocking the executor.
* **Decentralized UI & Onboarding**: Replaced hardcoded `dialoguer` prompts in the package manager with an Event Bus driven architecture. The OS Kernel now natively validates missing `.env.json` keys on startup and broadcasts `system.onboarding.required`. 
* **Native TUI Settings Menu**: The CLI natively intercepts onboarding events and dynamically renders an inline Settings Menu inside the Chat interface to elicit masked API keys and auto-refresh the background daemon.
* **Dynamic Slash Commands**: The TUI `/` palette is now dynamically injected over the Event Bus from the globally registered commands in loaded `Capsule.toml` manifests.

## Test Plan
1. Boot the OS daemon and open the chat frontend: `cargo run -p astrid-cli -- chat`
2. Install a new capsule inside the chat interface: `/install path/to/some.capsule`
3. Verify the native TUI Settings Menu overlay appears.
4. Input your requested secrets into the TUI prompt and press Enter.
5. Verify the `.env.json` is generated, the kernel hot-reloads, and the chat resumes automatically.

body:
### Motivation
- The previous fallback scanned `/sys/class/drm/*/modes` and could select the largest supported mode (e.g. 4K) instead of the currently active connector mode, causing `uxplay -s` to pass an oversized resolution and produce a tiny centered AirPlay window instead of true fullscreen.
- AirPlay should use the active display resolution across different hardware (Display HAT mini, HyperPixel variants, HDMI 1080p/4K and framebuffer-based displays) and the takeover daemon should behave consistently.

### Description
- Replaced the `/sys/class/drm/*/modes` aggregation with logic that locates connected DRM connectors by reading `status` and then reads the connector `mode` file to obtain the active resolution in `scripts/airplay_mode.sh`.
- Applied the same active-mode detection change to `scripts/airplay_takeover_daemon.sh` to make the always-on/background path consistent.
- Added an extra fallback that reads `/sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size` when present to support framebuffer-only displays.
- Kept the existing `xrandr` and `fbset` checks and added `awk` validation to ensure only well-formed `WIDTHxHEIGHT` strings are returned.

### Testing

author: joeshull
body:
## Summary

- Adds `.devcontainer/dc-exec`, a shell script that resolves the devcontainer from any git worktree using `git worktree list --porcelain` + Docker labels, then runs commands via `docker exec -w`
- Replaces all `devcontainer exec --workspace-folder .` references in CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, and evaluator prompts with `dc-exec` equivalents
- Unblocks parallel `/evaluate-tool` runs that use `EnterWorktree` for isolation

## How it works

`devcontainer exec` matches the host cwd to a `devcontainer.local_folder` Docker label. From a worktree (`.claude/worktrees/<name>/`), the cwd doesn't match, so container lookup fails. `dc-exec` instead:

1. Uses `git worktree list --porcelain` to find the main repo root (works from any worktree)
2. Finds the container via `docker ps --filter "label=devcontainer.local_folder=<repo-root>"`
3. Runs `docker exec -u vscode -w <workdir> <container> "$@"` with TTY detection

Supports `-C <dir>` flag for setting the container-side working directory.

## Test plan

- [ ] From main checkout: `.devcontainer/dc-exec python --version` succeeds
- [ ] From a worktree: `.devcontainer/dc-exec python --version` succeeds (same container)
- [ ] With `-C` flag: `.devcontainer/dc-exec -C /workspace/evaluations/pypsa uv run python -c "import pypsa"` works
- [ ] Run `/evaluate-tool pypsa` — gate tests execute from worktree context
- [ ] Verify pytest, julia, and octave commands all work from worktree

body:
Build a reverse index during indexing that tracks which definitions, references, and names depend on each `NameId`. Name-to-name edges encode the dependency type at registration time:

- `ChildName`: `parent_scope` relationship (structural dependency)
- `NestedName`: `nesting` relationship (reference-only dependency)
- `Definition/Reference`: direct dependents of the name

This index will be consumed by the incremental invalidation engine to efficiently cascade changes without scanning the full graph.

# Bug

<!-- If this is an engineering change or test change only, you do not need an issue. -->
<!-- Find or create an issue in NuGet/Home and paste the full url. -->
<!-- At the maintainers discretion, multiple changes may apply to a single issue, but only when the PRs are all created within a short period of time. -->
Fixes: https://github.com/nuget/home/issues/14788

## Description

When we changed the main parts of restore to use TargetAlias as the pivot instead of the NuGetFramework it basically meant that TargetAlias needs to either be empty or have a value. 

In many places in restore we default to empty if there's no value (non SDK projects) 

https://github.com/NuGet/NuGet.Client/blob/dev/src/NuGet.Core/NuGet.Commands/RestoreCommand/Utility/MSBuildRestoreUtility.cs#L445

https://github.com/NuGet/NuGet.Client/blob/dev/src/NuGet.Core/NuGet.Build.Tasks.Console/MSBuildStaticGraphRestore.cs#L734

In legacy PR, we don't set it.

In CPSPackageReference projects however, we set it, expecting that it's only invoked in SDK based scenarios but unfortunately that's not the case. 

Enter C++/CLI PackageReference hacks!

The confirmed scenario in question seems to be C++/CLI PackageReference (.NET Framework projects).

C++/CLI (.NET Core) supports PackageReference projects: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/cppblog/announcing-nuget-packagereference-support-for-c-cli-msbuild-projects-targeting-net-core/ . The way that works is the C++/CPS/project-system teams worked so that the nomination code from the managed lang system is being utilized to provide this restore data to NuGet. In the end for NuGet, while we did add some special compatibility rules, these restores appear the same as a normal SDK based project.

Note that native C++ PackageReference is not supported, https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Add-PackageReference-support-for-native-/10165376 . Similarly to many scenarios, it can work on the commandline, but project reference protocol and VS scenarios just won't work. Customers haven't really cared about that limitation.
They have been using all kinds of workarounds: [Use PackageReference in vcxproj - Developer Community](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/use-packagereference-in-vcxproj/351636#T-N10713858)  https://github.com/NuGet/Home/issues/8874 .

They basically set things like Capability, and all kinds of stuff to try to work around the implementation limiting when restore works.
These things are all unsupported. We have been clear about that, since not all scenarios are handled in C++ PackageReference today.
NuGet generates assets file, nuget.g.props, nuget.g.targets and none of those are guaranteed to be loaded or refreshed in these scenarios. So restore happens, but whether the build or intellisense actually works the way they wanted is not guaranteed.


That being said, this did get broken and the fix is rather straightforward, so we'll fix it, but we won't service stable, but insiders only. 

There is a workaround and that is setting the TargetFramework value.

sample nomination data for a C++/CLI project, https://github.com/jwfx/NuGetRestoreRepro/blob/master/Directory.Build.props.

author: hivemoot-worker
body:
Fixes #308

## What changed
- Reworked `retryTask` to re-queue the existing task in place instead of creating a new task ID.
- Added shared requeue logic that resets `created_at`/`updated_at` and clears terminal metadata when reviving to `pending`.
- Applied that timeout-reset behavior to all revive paths:
  - `retryTask`
  - `resumeTaskWithFollowUp`
  - terminal revival in `addUserMessage`
- Updated task detail retry UX to refresh in place when retry returns the same task id.
- Added/updated regression tests for:
  - stale `created_at` on follow-up resume
  - stale `created_at` on message-based terminal revive
  - in-place retry semantics and message-history preservation

## Why
Two user-facing bugs were linked:
1. revived tasks could immediately time out again because pending timeout checks were based on stale `created_at`
2. retry dropped message history by creating a brand-new task id

This change keeps task timeline continuity and starts a fresh timeout window for each re-queued attempt.

## Validation

author: ivanangelsegurafernandez
body:
### Motivation

- Migrate the feature contract to a new scalping-focused `CORE13_v2` to improve short-horizon signal quality and preserve compatibility with legacy bot outputs.
- Harden incremental dataset handling and ingestion to avoid corrupt/mutant CSVs, prevent bad rows, and backfill v2 features from legacy columns.
- Avoid deadlocks and lost continuity in martingala rotation by allowing a controlled, probability-gated repeat fallback for C2..C6 cycles. 
- Version IA artifacts and metadata so v2 experiments (model/scaler/features/meta) can coexist and be audited without mixing with legacy assets.

### Description

- Replaced `FEATURE_NAMES_CORE_13`, `FEATURE_SET_PROD_WARMUP`, and related feature sets with the new scalping `CORE13_v2` list and updated `INCREMENTAL_FEATURES_V2` to reuse it. 
- Added robust incremental processing: `_enriquecer_scalping_features_row` for legacy→v2 backfill, `clip_feature_values`, expanded `validar_fila_incremental` range checks, and improved `reparar_dataset_incremental_mutante` to prefer header-based mapping before positional rescue. 
- Introduced martingala continuity controls: new flags `MARTI_CYCLE_ALLOW_REPEAT_FALLBACK`, thresholds `MARTI_CYCLE_REPEAT_MIN_PROB*`, helper `_marti_repeat_min_prob_live`, and updated `elegir_candidato_rotacion_marti` and selection call sites to support controlled repeats only when operational probability meets the live threshold. 
- Versioned IA artifact paths to v2 (`_MODEL_PATH`, `_SCALER_PATH`, `_FEATURES_PATH`, `_META_PATH`), added `SCHEMA_VERSION_ACTIVE` and `DATASET_SCHEMA_TAG`, and include schema info in training `model_meta` saved by `maybe_retrain`. 
- Miscellaneous operational changes: disabled legacy gates/ranking during the transition (`GATE_SEGMENTO_ENABLED=False`, `PATTERN_V1_USE_HYBRID_RANKING=False`), ensured `oraculo_predict` enriches rows with v2 features at inference, updated reset/backfill/delete routines to consider v2 artifact names, and tightened HUD/gate readiness checks to avoid signaling when confirm/trigger states are incomplete.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this PR; please run unit and integration suites (import checks, incremental repair/backfill, `build_xy_from_incremental`, `oraculo_predict` and end-to-end canary flows) before promoting to production.

body:
The app had several layout breakages on mobile: toolbar buttons overflowed small viewports, the sidebar had no backdrop, the setup modal could exceed screen height, and iOS would auto-zoom on input focus.

## Changes

- **Toolbar:** New `@media (max-width: 640px)` rule shrinks record button (`140px → 110px`) and icon buttons (`40px → 36px`); hides audio visualizer to reclaim space. Added `toolbar-actions` class to replace brittle `:last-child` selector.
- **Sidebar:** Added `#sidebarOverlay` backdrop (`z-index: 1999`) with click-to-close. Replaced inline `onclick` toggle with `toggleSidebar()` function that syncs sidebar and overlay state. Fixed animation — overrides `transition: right 0.3s ease` in mobile media query (base rule only transitioned `width`).

author: xwolin
body:
## Problem
Three autonomous systems were running simultaneously:
1. **CortexEngine** — `cortexEngine.start()` in `main.ts` (think cycles every ~15 min)
2. **HeartbeatEngine** — `agentLoop.startHeartbeat(5min)` in `ipc.ts` (every 5 min)
3. **ProactiveEngine** — `proactiveEngine.start()` in `ipc.ts`

This caused **duplicate AI calls** every 5-15 minutes, double screen monitoring, and duplicate AFK detection logic.

## Fix (Phase 1 — safe)
Guard in `PROACTIVE_SET_MODE` handler: only start `HeartbeatEngine` when `CortexEngine` is **not** active (`cortexEnabled=false`).

When CortexEngine is enabled, it covers all autonomous think cycles, screen monitoring, and AFK management. HeartbeatEngine is preserved as a fallback for when CortexEngine is not configured.

## What's NOT changed
- HeartbeatEngine class stays (not deleted) — legacy fallback
- ProactiveEngine still starts (Phase 2 migration planned)
- No behavior change when CortexEngine is disabled

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 1682 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes

## Architecture decisions
- Decision #10: CortexEngine is primary autonomous brain
- Phase 2 (future): migrate ProactiveEngine rules into CortexEngine
- Phase 3 (future): delete HeartbeatEngine and ProactiveEngine classes

- Upgraded Werkzeug to 3.1.6 and pinned lxml to 5.3.0.

- Removed credential debug print and updated error logging to redact full response bodies in gartan_fetch.py.

author: nevinera
body:
Fixes #11 

This script makes it convenient to create, update, and append to a single slack thread from a persistent process. My target use-case is a CD master build:

* Create the message when the build starts, like `[🏗️ building] Release abcd1234 by @foo: Fram the Jumbiston carefully`
* Update it as the build passes through phases:
  - `[🧪 testing] Release abcd1234....`
  - `[🚀 deploying] Release abcd1234...`
  - `[✅ complete] Release abcd1234...`
  - Or if it reaches a failure state, `[❌ failed] Release abcd1234....`
* Add messages to the _thread_ (to avoid cluttering the channel) as each job fails, or in some cases succeeds:
  - `All builds completed after 7:03`
  - `Ruby Unit Tests failed on container 8`
  - `Deploys in progress: monolith, foo_service, bar_service`
  - `Failure encountered: "Could not fetch container ______ from dockerhub"`
* Update the readme to describe all three scripts in a new section, since they're intended for use.

In order to work with the same thread/message, we'll need to persist the artifact from job to job - in Circle/Github, that can be done with caches that include the current workflow ID in their keys (there are several ways really in github. And an s3 sidecar is a solid solution in almost any context).

author: jacobheric
body:
the old teardown executed all cleanup sql as a single statement. if any step failed (e.g. the replication slot was active, or a role had already been removed), the entire teardown would fail and leave resources behind. this made it impossible for users to remove and re-add their CDC integration. They'd  then get  errors like: `replication slot "inngest_cdc" is active for PID <N (SQLSTATE 55006)"` and get stuck.

 **Changes**

  - execute each teardown step individually so that a failure in one step (e.g. role already removed) doesn't block the rest of the cleanup.
  - handle active replication slots by checking pg_replication_slots for an active PID, calling pg_terminate_backend(), and retrying the slot drop after a brief delay if needed.
  - add defer conn.Close(ctx) to avoid leaking the teardown connection.
  - best-effort cleanup for non-critical resources — privilege revocations and user/publication drops log warnings but don't fail the overall teardown if the resource is already gone.

**_NOTE_**: I vendored this into monorepo locally and tested it e2e against various failures scenarios with neon and supabase.

body:
- 20x for DEBUG 20x for RELEASE improvement in image comparison
- Use low-level coding techniques to calculate tile signatures faster


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Replaces a core image-diff primitive with new low-level C/NEON code and unsafe buffer plumbing, which could affect correctness or stability of session replay capture if edge cases slip through.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Major perf change:** Tile signature generation used for image diffs is rewritten to use a new `SessionReplayC` target (C + optional ARM NEON), replacing the prior Swift/CommonCrypto SHA-256 per-tile hashing with a faster non-crypto 128-bit style hash and centralized tile layout computation.
> 
> `TileSignatureManager` now calls `tile_compute_layout`/`tile_compute_all` and reuses an internal C buffer; `ImageSignature` is split into its own file and now precomputes an accumulated hash to speed dictionary lookups/equality.
> 
> **Validation/benchmarking:** Adds `TileHashParityTests` to ensure NEON and scalar paths match, updates the benchmark tooling/UI to measure signature computation, and forces decoded frame images in `RawFrameReader` for more consistent pixel access. Packaging is updated so CocoaPods and SPM both build/link the new `SessionReplayC` module.

## Summary of fixes

### 🔴 Production CORS failures (all API calls blocked)
- `FRONTEND_URL` in `render.yaml` was the internal Render URL (`options-tax-hub-client-prod.onrender.com`), but browsers send `Origin: https://www.optionstaxhub.com` (custom domain after www-redirect) → CORS preflight blocked every request

- `get_supabase_with_token` passed the user JWT as the Supabase API key — rejected by Kong gateway, so all PostgREST history reads silently returned empty
